planning_scheme.name: Burke Shire Planning Scheme 2020
planning_scheme.notes: Citation and commencement (PDF p.2): "This planning scheme may be cited as Burke Shire Planning Scheme 2020. A notice was published in the Government Gazette No.20 on 31 January 2020 for the planning scheme for the Shire of Burke. The commencement date for the planning scheme was 7 February 2020." Council planning page (per earlier check; www host returns 403 to scripts) states the scheme was "adopted by Council at the January 2020 and has a commencement date of 7 February 2020"; no version/amendment number is published. The official PDF is served from a pre-production (OpenCities "prelive") host, burkeshire.prelive.opencities.com, which the council planning page itself links; www.burke.qld.gov.au returns 403 to scripts. QHC: the scheme (2020) does not mention the Queensland Housing Code; no QHC adoption found (text search for "Housing Code" returns nothing). Printed page numbers equal PDF page numbers.

qdc_qhc_relationship.summary: Section 1.6 states the scheme regulates building work through Part 5 under ss32-33 of the Building Act 1975, and an editor's note says the Act permits alternative boundary clearance provisions for Class 1 and 10 structures (s33). However the scheme does not designate any specific provision as a QDC alternative provision, and Table 5.8 (building work) only captures building work at local heritage places and in airport operational airspace. There is no dwelling house code. Class 10 boundary clearances on dwelling house lots therefore default to the QDC (MP1.1/MP1.2), except where a dwelling house MCU is code assessable and zone code AO1 (Rural, Rural residential) applies. No QHC adoption.

quotes.text: Section 17(b) of the Regulation identifies the assessment benchmarks for building work that a local planning instrument must not change the effect to the extent the building work is regulated under the building assessment provisions, unless permitted under the Building Act 1975.
This planning scheme, through Part 5, regulates building work in accordance with Sections 32 and 33 of the Building Act 1975.

Editor’s note—the Building Act 1975 permits planning schemes to: • regulate, for the Building Code of Australia (BCA) or the Queensland Development Code (QDC), matters prescribed under a regulation under the Building Act 1975 (section 32). For example, building height and space for on-site parking. It may also regulate other matters such as designating floor levels of habitable rooms in flood areas, designating areas as being subject to bushfire hazard, noise corridors and end-of-trip facilities; • deal with an aspect of, or matter related or incidental to building work prescribed under a regulation under Section 32 of the Building Act 1975; • specify alternative design solutions for boundary clearance and site cover provisions for Class 1 and 10 structures under Section 33 of the Building Act 1975.

definitions.text: A residential use of premises for one household that contains a single dwelling. The use includes domestic outbuildings and works normally associated with a dwelling and may include a secondary dwelling.

A Class 10a building, as defined in the Building Code of Australia, that is ancillary to a residential use on the same premises and is limited to non-habitable buildings for the purpose of a shed, garage and carport.

A building or part of a building used or capable of being used as a self-contained residence that must include the following: (a) food preparation facilities (b) a bath or shower (c) a toilet and wash basin (d) clothes washing facilities. This term includes outbuildings, structures and works normally associated with a dwelling.
For a building or structure, the shortest distance measured horizontally from the outer most projection of a building or structure to the vertical projection of the boundary of the lot.

rules.notes: Dwelling house is accepted development subject to requirements against the General development code only (Township Residential precinct; Rural residential; Rural if <=2 dwellings, not bushfire prone, no abandoned mine). The only GDC part for accepted development subject to requirements is PO1/AO1 (flood). Township Commercial and Industrial precincts: dwelling house is code assessable against Township zone code + GDC, neither of which states a front setback for a dwelling house. Table 5.8: building work (e.g. a shed added later) is accepted development except for local heritage places and airport operational airspace, so no council setback applies to Class 10 building work.

rules.alternative_provision_to_qdc_qhc: NO - not designated as a QDC alternative provision (s1.6(3) / Table 5.8 regulate building work only for heritage and airport airspace). AO5 applies only to assessable development for uses other than Dwelling houses, Dual occupancies and Multiple dwellings.
rules.notes: Applies via General development code AO5 (Table 7.2.1.1, under the headings "For assessable development" and "All uses excluding Dwelling houses, Dual occupancies and Multiple dwellings"). It therefore does NOT reach domestic outbuildings (sheds, garages, carports) of a Dwelling house; it reaches Class 10 buildings/structures only when part of another assessable use (e.g. caretaker's accommodation, home based business, non-residential uses). AO5 yields to a zone code prescription ("Unless otherwise prescribed in a zone code"). Site coverage and height columns omitted from verbatim_text (out of scope). Corresponding AO5 text: PO5 Buildings and structures are setback from the front, side and rear boundaries generally consistent with: • the intended form, function and character of development in the respective zone or zone precinct; and • prevailing setbacks of existing development in the same zone or zone precinct in the locality; and • amenity outcomes for adjoining development, streetscapes and public spaces. | AO5 Unless otherwise prescribed in a zone code, or other Acceptable outcome within the General development code, development provides setbacks in accordance with Table 7.2.1.4 – Building heights, setbacks and site coverage.

local_plan_mechanism.summary: The scheme has no local plans and no overlay codes (natural hazards are handled inside the General development code and Schedule 2 mapping). Township zone has three precincts (Commercial, Residential, Industrial) set in the Township zone code and Table 7.2.1.4.

open_questions: The official PDF is hosted on a pre-production OpenCities host (burkeshire.prelive.opencities.com) linked from the council planning page; confirm with council that this is the current authoritative copy and whether a production-host URL exists (www.burke.qld.gov.au returns 403 to scripts).
No version/amendment number is published; confirm no amendments since commencement on 7 February 2020.

Table 7.2.1.4 setbacks apply via AO5 only to assessable development for uses other than Dwelling houses, Dual occupancies and Multiple dwellings; confirm curators should not apply them to dwelling house outbuildings.
Township Commercial precinct AO12.1 (2m from a residential precinct boundary) technically reaches a code-assessable dwelling house in that precinct; confirm whether to apply to Class 10.
Rural zone: zone code AO1 front setback (6m) conflicts with Table 7.2.1.4 (10m); AO5 defers to the zone code.
No provision is expressly designated a QDC alternative provision under s33 despite the s1.6 editor's note; confirm council's position.
